verified.exploit_entry_point: The library's public resolution API. A validating resolver is built with Resolver::builder_with_config(..).with_trust_anchor(..).build(); a downstream caller invokes Resolver::lookup(name, type) or Resolver::lookup_ip(name). The scripted upstream returns unsigned records for which no chain of trust to the configured trust anchor can be established, so validation marks the answer as not-Secure. On the vulnerable code the call returns Ok with those records (proof=Bogus); on fixed code it returns an error.
variants: Resolver::lookup(name, RecordType::A) on a positive answer that fails validation (lookup()/LookupFuture path).
Resolver::lookup(name, RecordType::TXT) on a positive answer that fails validation (same path, different record class).
Resolver::lookup_ip(name) on a positive answer that fails validation (distinct LookupIpFuture path, NOT routed through Resolver::lookup()).
Resolver::lookup_ip(second name) on a positive answer that fails validation (same distinct path, confirms it is not tied to one input).
verified.variant_coverage_note: lookup() and lookup_ip() do not share the public method: lookup_ip() builds LookupIpFuture directly, so a fix applied only inside Resolver::lookup() leaves both lookup_ip variants exploitable. The upstream fix sits at the common CachingClient::lookup sink, covering all four.
services: none (in-process scripted upstream via test-support MockProvider; no sockets, no network)
verified.project_tests_run: The crate's own resolver tests for this area query real public resolvers (Cloudflare/Google) and cannot run in a no-network image, so they were not executed. Instead the behavior change was validated with an in-process mock harness that mirrors the upstream fix commit's own added regression test (test_dnssec_validation_bogus_fails): confirmed to return Ok(records) on the vulnerable parent commit and an error on the fix commit, both via cargo nextest. Oracle fix.patch (source-only subset) makes all 9 tests pass; vulnerable makes all 4 security tests fail and all 5 functional tests pass.

notes: Rust workspace; DNSSEC validation enabled via trust anchors. The fix.patch is the upstream commit reduced to source files (net error type, retry handle, resolver caching client, server forwarder); the upstream test-only hunks (resolver.rs test module, conformance bogus.rs) were dropped. Tests run against the harness crate baked at /opt/harness with a shared pre-built CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/opt/target and CARGO_HOME=/opt/cargo, so a verifier run recompiles only the patched /app crates. No network at run time.
